sources.title: Baidu interview note containing the equal-sum split prompt
Answer Batch 0019 mechanically extracted repository-source packet
Deterministic Java validation against exhaustive subset enumeration oracle
Source-first isolated review for the equal-sum partition candidate

claims.text: The retained repository source asks whether an array can be split into two arrays whose element sums are equal; it does not require contiguous subarrays or specify sign/range, non-empty groups, language, null handling, or an API shape.

Java int[] input, non-negative elements, total sum <= Integer.MAX_VALUE, complete element partition, empty-group allowance, and null=false are explicit candidate choices rather than recovered prompt facts.
Under the chosen complete-partition contract, two equal-sum groups exist exactly when the total is even and some subset sums to half of the total.
For one-dimensional 0/1 subset-sum DP, descending target iteration prevents the current element from being reused in the same round.
For target T = total/2, the selected dynamic program uses O(nT) time and O(T) auxiliary space and is pseudo-polynomial in numeric magnitude.
The exact Java fixture passes 10 fixed cases and 5000 deterministic randomized arrays against an exhaustive subset-enumeration oracle while confirming the input is unchanged.

boundary_tests.expected: false because two equal integer sums require an even total
true under the explicit candidate contract that permits empty groups
dynamic-program result matches exhaustive subset oracle without mutation

findings: The retained repository source asks only whether one array can be split into two arrays/groups with equal element sums; the candidate does not reintroduce contiguous-subarray semantics.

Because the source does not define sign/range, non-empty-group rules, language, null behavior, or API shape, the candidate labels Java int[], non-negative values, total-sum bound, empty-group allowance, and null behavior as candidate choices.
Under the chosen complete-partition contract, equal partition is equivalent to existence of a subset summing to half of the total; odd totals therefore fail immediately.
The descending one-dimensional update is correct for 0/1 element use and avoids the same-round reuse bug that an ascending update would introduce.
The candidate explicitly calls O(nT) time and O(T) space pseudo-polynomial and does not claim source-backed optimality in the absence of input limits.
The exact Java fixture was independently executed with OpenJDK 21.0.11 and produced 'PASS fixed=10 randomized=5000 oracle=exhaustive-subset-partition mutation=none'.
No production or personal experience is fabricated; formal promotion remains blocked by the repository human-approval gate.
